subject: Fleet slot negotiation: private vs reserved capacity breakdown
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@meddynamics.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@meddynamics.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private vs Reserved capacity for regulated workloads — initial ask

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Meddynamics is moving fast on a regulated pilot (PHI + some PII) and we need a clear decision brief for the exec team on hosting posture. Specifically:

- Can you provide a head-to-head summary of Private (VPC / on-prem package) vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for our workload?
- We need committed slot sizing (GPU counts and expected QPS/tokens) for an initial 6-month pilot and for a scale-to-prod 12-month plan.
- Procurement timeline constraints: we need firm lead times for on-prem OOB vs reserved pool activation.
- Any compliance evidence we should include (SOC2 snapshots, audit logs, KMS integration notes).

Happy to share a usage sample and current token-per-call profile if that helps. Procurement is cc'd — they likely will ask for a price band and conversion options (reserved -> private).

Looking for a short playbook we can present on Wed Exec sync.

Appreciate it,
Dana
Head of ML Ops
Meddynamics

(Attachment: med_workload_sample.csv)

From: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private vs Reserved capacity for regulated workloads — initial ask

Dana — thanks for the clear list. I'll assemble a concise two-page decision brief + a sizing worksheet for the execs. To make the sizing concrete, can you confirm two quick points from the workload sample:

1) Typical request shape: mean tokens per call and 95th percentile tokens.
2) Percent of calls that require model variants with long-context (>=8k) vs short-context.

High level on our side: we typically recommend starting with a small Reserved (Dedicated) pool to enable fast time-to-value, with an option to >>convert<< to Private if you need on-prem or air-gapped control. The main tradeoffs are:
- Dedicated: faster onboarding (1–2 weeks to provision committed slots), predictable throughput, lower up-front engineering.
- Private: stronger isolation, customer-managed network and keys, longer lead time (~6–10 weeks on average for on-prem or VPC private control plane).

I'm attaching a draft SOW and the commitment tier spreadsheet — will fill in the recommended counts once we have the token distributions. Karthik, can you sketch the GPU mix for Meddynamics' sample (A100 vs H100, quantization assumptions)?

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private vs Reserved capacity for regulated workloads — initial ask

Dana / Priya — quick technical breakdown based on the sample (thanks for sending). I'll keep it short:

Summary assumptions from sample: mean tokens/call = 620, p95 tokens = 2,300. ~22% of calls use long-context models (context >= 8k). Average QPS observed (steady) = 3rps, burst p99 = 12rps.

Recommended initial pilot sizing (6 months, conservative):
- Dedicated (Reserved) lane: 4x H100-80GB equiv slots (continuous), 2x burst-capable H100s for p99 spikes. Expected sustained throughput ~9k tokens/sec with KV caching, tail latency SLO ~150–220ms for short-context models.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 3x H100-80GB + 2x A100-80GB (for cost-mix and mixed-precision workloads) to support long-context batch pipelines; plan for dedicated networking, KMS endpoint, and on-prem install window.

Conversion & procurement notes:
- Provisioning time: Dedicated reserved pool activation = 7–10 business days after contract + payment.
- Private (VPC control plane + on-prem delivery): typical lead = 6–9 weeks (includes DSAR/KMS onboarding, infra scheduling, and on-site remote install for air-gapped).
- Cost delta: Private on-prem capex + integration premium ≈ 25–40% over equivalent Dedicated monthly run-rate in year 1 (depends on hardware choice and local ops).

Operational suggestions:
- Start pilot on Dedicated (fast), enable prefix/KV caching and batching policies. If you hit isolation/regulatory gating, we can schedule private migration and preserve identical model versions — stateful migration is supported via model pinning and KV export.
- If procurement needs a conversion ladder, we recommend a 3-month reserved commitment with a conversion credit applied toward Private onboarding fees.

Link to internal fleet sizing calc: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/fleet-sizing-calc-4721 (read-only)

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement asks: can you give price bands for the two commitment tiers (3-month reserved pilot, 12-month reserved; and equivalent Private onboarding + 12-month support)? We don't need final redlines yet, just ballpark bands to include in the exec pack.
- Engineering asks: is there a recommended fallback plan if we outgrow reserved burst capacity mid-quarter? Can we auto-burst into a mixed-tenant fallback tier briefly? What are latency implications?
- Compliance asks: can you provide the SOC2 snapshot and a short one-pager listing audit/log retention, KMS integration expectations, and how we can validate isolation?

Procurement also noted they prefer a stepwise conversion credit (apply up to 50% of unused reserved commit toward Private onboarding if converted within 6 months). Is that something Redwood typically offers?

We have an internal exec sync on Wed 11:00 PT — if you can provide a 2-slide brief + price bands before then, that would be ideal.

Dana

Dana / team — attached are the two-slide decision brief and the requested price bands (ballpark). Highlights:

- Timeline: Reserved Dedicated pool provisioning = 7–10 business days after signed order. Private (VPC + on-prem option) typical lead = 6–9 weeks; air-gapped on-prem adds ~2 weeks for shipping and onsite validation.
- Commitment options we propose to include in the exec pack:
  * Option A (Pilot, Reserved - 3 month): 4 H100-equivalent slots, burst pool enabled (2 burst H100). Monthly run-rate = $XXX,XXX (ballpark). Conversion credit up to 50% of unused reserved commit if converted within 6 months.
  * Option B (Reserved - 12 month): same base with deeper discount, monthly run-rate = $YYY,YYY. Includes 2 free migration credits for Private onboarding (covers project PM + initial ops).
  * Option C (Private On-Prem): Capex + integration fee (one-time) = $ZZZ,ZZZ, ongoing support/op costs (monthly) = $WWW,WWW. We can structure as purchase+support or a managed Private subscription.

- Fallback: we support automated fallback to multi-tenant burst lanes for short durations; latency for fallbacks depends on model context size (typical +30–80ms for short-context; for long-context, cache warm-up may add 150–400ms momentarily). We can add a pre-warm policy to reduce impact.
- Compliance pack: attached SOC2 snapshot and KMS integration notes.

Next step: please confirm which option you want presented to the execs (A/B/C) and whether procurement would like a draft SOW + payment terms prior to Wed 11:00 PT. If you want, Marissa and I can join the exec call to walk the slides.

Thanks — Priya
